findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value (e.g. "sent", "deleted", "f00b4r"), making illegal packet states constructible at compile time.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code can branch on status == "sent" but the struct could hold any string, causing undefined workflow behavior or silent data corruption.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a sealed enum `PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` so only valid states are representable.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive flag that can be set independently of status, allowing contradictory states (e.g. status="sent" with is_validated=false).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state combinations are constructible; the workflow invariant (validated before sent) cannot be enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Collapse bool flags into a single typestate enum (e.g. `PacketStatus`) where the valid progression is encoded in the type.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a primitive flag that duplicates information from status and can diverge (is_sent=true with status!="sent").
findings.failure_mode: Contradictory state (e.g. is_sent=true but status="pending") is representable, causing inconsistent downstream decisions.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent` entirely; derive send status from the `PacketStatus` enum (e.g. `PacketStatus::Sent`). If a timestamp is needed, attach it as a field on the enum variant.

findings.problem: id: String is a bare primitive with no domain invariants (length, format, uniqueness).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs (empty, duplicate, malformed) propagate through the workflow without detection at the boundary.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `PacketId(String)` with a fallible constructor that validates format/length, and use it in `PacketWorkflow`.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns PacketWorkflow by value, mutating the struct in place rather than returning a new immutable state.
findings.failure_mode: No immutable-by-default guarantees; callers can hold a mutable reference and create inconsistent intermediate states.
findings.fix: Change to `fn mark_sent(item: &PacketWorkflow) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, TransitionError>` that returns a new validated state, enforcing the transition invariant.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a heap String on every call for a value that is always the same literal.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition; violates the performance discipline to avoid cargo-culted allocations.
findings.fix: After converting `status` to an enum, no allocation is needed. The variant is a zero-cost compile-time constant.

findings.problem: PacketWorkflow exposes all fields as pub with no constructor, so any code can instantiate it with arbitrary values bypassing invariants.
findings.failure_mode: The structural invariant (id present, status in valid set, validated before sent) cannot be enforced; callers bypass all domain rules.
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide a `PacketWorkflow::new(id: PacketId) -> Self` constructor, and expose only read-only accessors. Use a transition method or builder for state changes.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied performance characteristics
no profiler data to measure allocation patterns in mark_sent
no allocation audit for the to_string() path under load
no command-line entry point or CLI demonstration of the workflow
no behavior tests covering state transitions or invalid state rejection
residual_risk: The struct represents illegal states freely (any status string, independent bool flags, no constructor). Without enum-based typestates and a closed constructor, the domain model cannot guarantee workflow invariants at compile time. Static review only; no commands run.
